result:
I graded submission s2 and saved the grades to `grades/0001-s2.json`. You got 3 of 6 fully right.

| Item | Verdict | Feedback |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | Correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | Correct | The model only outputs a request naming the tool. This was wrong in your first attempt. |
| q3 | Wrong | A step limit is the safeguard. The agent gets no new information on each pass, so running longer will not fix the bug. This is misconception M6. |
| q4 | Partial | 4 is the right count. But you wrote that the model runs the tools itself, and that is misconception M4. The model only requests a tool, and your program runs it. |
| q5 | Correct | You gave both parts: the result goes back as the next input, and the model uses it to decide its next step. |
| q6 | Partial | The model chooses from each tool's description (name, purpose and parameters), not from the name alone. Your first attempt said this better. |

I also added `learning-records/0003-model-requests-program-runs.md` and updated `NOTES.md`. I didn't grade `submissions/s1.json`, since you only asked for s2.

**Next step:** redraw your laser cutter trace with two columns, "model outputs" and "program does". Mark where a step limit would stop the loop. Then we can move on to context and memory.

Do you want a short lesson on writing tool descriptions? It would fix q6 and is part of your mission.
